finalists.label: Sister Mary Joseph nodule
finalists.why: This candidate has the most specific and direct evidence from the vignette, including a firm nodule at the umbilicus and biopsy demonstrating adenocarcinoma.

finalists.label: Adenocarcinoma
finalists.why: This candidate is supported by the biopsy results showing well-differentiated, infiltrating adenocarcinoma, which is a key finding in the vignette.

frontier_selector.why: The champion is chosen because it specifically accounts for the umbilical nodule and its characteristics, which are unique findings in the vignette.

support_spans: a firm nodule at the umbilicus that gradually increased in size and became ulcerated and tender
the umbilical lesion measured 6 cm by 6 cm, was ulcerated over its entire surface, and bled on contact
Biopsy of the umbilical lesion demonstrated a well-differentiated, infiltrating adenocarcinoma
Deep palpation of the abdomen revealed a poorly defined, firm mass approximately 8 cm in diameter in the right hypochondrium

Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT showed homogeneously enhancing umbilical tissue growth and irregular, circumferential thickening of the right third of the transverse colon measuring approximately 8.3 cm
contradict_spans: Total colonoscopy revealed no endoluminal lesion
